name: Tatar
notes:
Tatar in Cyrillic script (Tatarstan). Nine vowels with front/back harmony: а /a/, ә /æ/, о /o/, ө /ø/, у /u/, ү /y/, ы /ɯ/, и /i/, е /e/ (values per Berta 1998, "Tatar and Bashkir", in The Turkic Languages, Johanson & Csató eds.; edition not consulted this session, standard Turkological description; orthographic inventory per Wikipedia, "Tatar alphabet"). Ә, Ө, Ү are Cyrillic letters with descenders/hooks, not the Latin ə ö ü they resemble.

Tatar Cyrillic has no distinct letter for the uvular fricative/stop: г spells both /ɡ/ and /ʁ/, and к both /k/ and /q/, conditioned by front/back vowel harmony (Berta 1998). The convention that marks the back (uvular) reading is the digraphs ⟨гъ⟩ and ⟨къ⟩ (ъ after г/к signals /ʁ/, /q/ rather than its own glottal value); that digraph rule is left unmodeled here — г and к are given their plain (front-harmony) values only, and ъ/ь keep their independent glottal candidate below regardless of context. This is a documented residual pending a primary-source wave, not a silent deletion, since г/к still surface as segments.

Җ is a Tatar-specific letter, the voiced alveolo-palatal fricative /ʑ/, distinct from Ж /ʒ/ (Berta 1998). Ң = /ŋ/, Һ = /h/.

Ъ and Ь mark [ʔ] (glottal stop/glottalization) per Wikipedia, "Tatar alphabet"; a silent reading is kept as a secondary candidate for the minority of tokens where they are orthographic-only. Ё /jo/ and Ц /ts/, Щ /ʃtʃ/, В /v/ carry Russian loanwords.

stress.notes: Tatar default stress is word-final (-1). Certain suffixes (negation, question particle) and borrowed words carry non-final stress; lexical and not modeled here. Source: Comrie (1997), Johanson & Csató (1998).
